title: Stocks vs Real Estate vs Business: Which Builds Wealth Faster
description:
Stocks, real estate or a business: which one builds wealth faster? In this video I put all three side by side from three angles: the numbers (long-run returns, leverage, failure rates, costs, taxes and time), the psychology that pulls people toward one path, and a playbook for choosing and combining them at every stage of life.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:50 How we got the numbers
2:24 Angle 1: The Numbers
2:30 1. Stocks: the long run engine
4:15 2. Real estate: rent plus growth
5:54 3. Leverage
7:30 4. Business: highest ceiling, highest risk
9:01 5. Costs and friction
10:25 6. Taxes
11:55 7. Time and liquidity
13:29 Angle 2: The Psychology
13:45 8. The comfort of something you can touch
15:01 9. Invisible volatility
16:15 10. Survivorship bias
17:37 11. What you enjoy matters
18:47 12. Risk and sleep
19:53 13. Concentration versus diversification
21:04 14. Family stories
22:32 Angle 3: The Playbook
22:42 15. Build the stock base first
23:48 16. Your home is a home first
24:50 17. Try real estate the easy way
26:01 18. Start a business small
27:06 19. Combine them
28:08 20. Choose by your stage
29:19 Three friends
30:35 Questions people ask
32:23 Mistakes on each path
33:36 Recap
34:12 What to do next

Sources:
- Jorda, Knoll, Kuvshinov, Schularick and Taylor, The Rate of Return on Everything, 1870-2015 (Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2019)
- Robert Shiller, Irrational Exuberance: long-run U.S. home prices adjusted for inflation
- S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index
- S&P Dow Jones Indices: S&P 500 long-run total returns
- U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics: establishment survival rates
- Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances: business equity among wealthiest households
- IRS: depreciation, 1031 exchanges, home sale exclusion, retirement plans for the self-employed
- Morgan Housel, The Psychology of Money (2020)
- Growth examples: monthly compounding at stated average yearly returns (illustrations, not promises)

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video37.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
